description_good_justification: README.md opens with a clear one-line description ('A domain-general, multi-model reasoning system for debate, proof, research, invention, and verified implementation.') plus a longer explanation and a 'Why Crosstalk' section; GitHub repo description field also set ('Metacognitive multi-agent AI orchestrator...').
interact_justification: README.md has an 'Install' section (git clone / cargo build) and CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to submit issues/PRs and set up a dev environment; SECURITY.md and SUPPORT.md give feedback channels.
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'How to Contribute' section explains topic branches, PR process, required CI gate (cargo fmt/clippy/test), and PR template at .github/pull_request_template.md.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md specifies coding style (rustfmt.toml, clippy -D warnings), commit message convention (Conventional Commits), and a 'Security-Sensitive Code' section with extra review requirements for src/engines/security.rs, src/mcp/, src/engines/sandbox.rs.
floss_license_justification: Repo is licensed Apache-2.0 (LICENSE file, Cargo.toml `license = "Apache-2.0"`, GitHub API licenseInfo.key = "apache-2.0").
license_location_justification: Full Apache-2.0 text is at /Volumes/A/crosstalk/LICENSE (repo root, standard location), and referenced from README.md and Cargo.toml.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md (~20K) covers install, quick start, capability status table, architecture pipeline diagram; docs/ directory has 8 further documents (general-intelligence.md, evaluation.md, formal-verification.md, discovery-workbench.md, etc.).
documentation_interface_justification: docs/ contains reference material for the CLI/API surface (e.g. docs/evaluation.md, docs/formal-verification.md, docs/general-intelligence.md) and README documents CLI usage (`crosstalk --help`, `--generate-completions`, `--audit-only --cases`); CONTRIBUTING.md requires CLI examples be kept synced with `crosstalk --help`.
sites_https_justification: Project is hosted at https://github.com/dcondrey/crosstalk (GitHub serves all pages over HTTPS/TLS); all README links use https:// URLs.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled (`gh repo view` -> hasIssuesEnabled: true) at https://github.com/dcondrey/crosstalk/issues, is URL-addressable, searchable, and open to any GitHub user with no proprietary client required.
english_justification: All documentation (README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, docs/*.md, code comments) is in English.
maintained_justification: `git log` shows commits as recently as 2026-08-20 (`cfa1f6f chore: remove case-colliding PR template`, `ae89076 feat: build verifiable general discovery platform`) and GitHub API pushedAt = 2026-08-24T13:11:29Z, both well within the last 60 days as of 2026-08-26.
repo_public_justification: `gh repo view dcondrey/crosstalk` reports visibility: PUBLIC, isPrivate: false, at https://github.com/dcondrey/crosstalk.
repo_track_justification: Git (via `.git/`) records full authorship, timestamps, and diffs for every commit; verified with `git log --format='%an %ad %s'` showing author, date, and message per commit.
repo_interim_justification: `git log --oneline` shows many incremental commits between any notion of releases (e.g. dozens of feat/fix/docs commits since project inception on 2026-06-21 through 2026-08-20), not just release snapshots.
repo_distributed_justification: Repository uses Git, a distributed VCS (`.git/` present, remote `origin` at git@github.com:dcondrey/crosstalk.git).
version_unique_justification: Cargo.toml declares `version = "0.1.0"`, a unique SemVer identifier for the package; CHANGELOG.md is structured by version per Keep a Changelog format.
version_semver_justification: Cargo.toml version `0.1.0` follows SemVer (required by Cargo itself); CHANGELOG.md explicitly follows the Keep a Changelog + SemVer/Conventional Commits convention.
version_tags_justification: `git tag -l` returns no output — no version tags exist in the repository yet, even though Cargo.toml is at 0.1.0 and CI has release-on-tag logic (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` triggers a release job on `refs/tags/v*`) that has not yet been exercised.
release_notes_justification: No discrete GitHub Releases exist yet (`gh release list` returned empty) and no git tags exist; project has not cut a first tagged release, so this criterion is not yet applicable. CHANGELOG.md currently only has an '[Unreleased]' section.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No releases have been made yet (see release_notes), so there are no release notes to identify fixed vulnerabilities in.
report_process_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled with structured templates at .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml and feature_request.yml, and .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml disables blank issues and points security reports to SECURITY.md / GitHub Security Advisories.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues (per-issue tracker with templates) is used, at https://github.com/dcondrey/crosstalk/issues.
report_responses_justification: No qualifying reports exist to assess a majority against (evidence: `gh issue list --repo dcondrey/crosstalk --state all` returns zero issues filed to date, so there are no unacknowledged bug reports in the last 2-12 months (vacuously satisfied). Repo is young (created 2026-06-21) with a single active maintainer who also owns CODEOWNERS review.). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met — flag for maintainer confirmation if/when real reports arrive.
enhancement_responses_justification: No qualifying enhancement requests exist to assess a majority against (evidence: Same evidence as report_responses: no enhancement requests have been filed yet (`gh issue list` empty), so none are unaddressed.). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues at https://github.com/dcondrey/crosstalk/issues is a publicly available, searchable archive of any reports and responses (currently empty but publicly browsable).
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents a full 'Reporting a Vulnerability' process (email admin@writerslogic.com, required info, response timeline, coordinated disclosure policy); also linked from .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md instructs private reporting via email (admin@writerslogic.com) and .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml links to GitHub's private 'Security Vulnerability' advisory form at https://github.com/dcondrey/crosstalk/security/advisories/new.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received (no security advisories or issues on record), so there is no response-time data to evaluate for the last 6 months.
build_justification: Project builds with `cargo build` / `cargo build --release` as documented in README.md 'Install' and CONTRIBUTING.md 'Development Setup'; Cargo.toml defines a workspace with 3 members and 3 binaries built automatically by Cargo, a standard FLOSS build tool.
build_common_tools_justification: Uses Cargo, the standard Rust build tool, with no custom/nonstandard build wrapper; .github/workflows/ci.yml invokes `cargo check`/`cargo build` directly.
build_floss_tools_justification: Entire toolchain is FLOSS: rustc/Cargo (MIT/Apache-2.0), dtolnay/rust-toolchain GitHub Action, and all crates.io dependencies; no proprietary compiler or SDK is required per Cargo.toml or ci.yml.
test_justification: 39 automated test files exist under tests/ (e.g. tests/algorithm_discovery_tests.rs, tests/consensus_tests.rs, tests/deliberation_tests.rs) plus unit tests in src/; CONTRIBUTING.md documents running them via `cargo test --workspace`, and CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs `cargo test --lib --workspace` and `cargo test --workspace --test '*' --doc`.
test_invocation_justification: Tests are invoked with the standard Rust convention `cargo test --workspace`, documented identically in CONTRIBUTING.md and used in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
test_most_justification: 39 integration test files under tests/ covering distinct subsystems (algorithm_discovery, analytics, auditor, consensus, constraint_routing, deliberation, environment, etc.) plus unit tests inline in src/, indicating broad functional coverage across the codebase's major modules.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `cargo check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, and `cargo test` on every push to any branch and every PR to main, across a 3-OS matrix (macos-14, ubuntu-latest, windows-latest).
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Making Changes' step 4 states: 'Add a regression test for every fix or new behavior where feasible.'
tests_are_added_justification: CHANGELOG.md/`git log` show test additions accompanying feature work (e.g. commit history entries like 'QualityTrendDetector...29 new tests', 'BudgetManager...20 new tests', 'MemoryBridge with cross-session recall, SessionContext, 11 new tests', 'SurpriseEngine...11 new tests'), consistent with the stated policy being followed.
tests_documented_added_justification: The test-addition policy is documented directly in CONTRIBUTING.md under 'Making Changes' (see test_policy).
warnings_justification: clippy (the standard FLOSS Rust linter) is run in CI via `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` in .github/workflows/ci.yml, and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is required per CONTRIBUTING.md.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI enforces `-D warnings` (turns clippy warnings into hard failures) on every push/PR in .github/workflows/ci.yml, so the build cannot merge with outstanding warnings; CHANGELOG.md also records a historical entry 'fix all clippy warnings'.
warnings_strict_justification: CI uses `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, which denies (fails the build on) all default clippy lint warnings across the whole workspace and all targets, a maximally strict practical setting for Rust.
know_secure_design_justification: SECURITY.md 'Security Model' documents an explicit threat model and design (workspace-confined tool gateway rejecting path traversal, allow-listed shell_exec, WASM sandbox with fuel/memory/timeout limits, ed25519-signed transcripts with pinned public keys, hash-chain tamper evidence, sandboxed proof checkers) showing deliberate secure-design practice by the primary developer.
know_common_errors_justification: SECURITY.md explicitly discusses mitigations for common classes of errors relevant to this software: path traversal (`..`/`~`/absolute-path rejection), prompt injection screening on untrusted model/tool output, command-injection prevention in shell_exec (metacharacter/control-char rejection), and secret handling (`Zeroizing` buffers, 'never logged'), plus CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Security-Sensitive Code' section warning against custom crypto and log leakage.
crypto_published_justification: SECURITY.md 'Cryptographic Primitives' lists only publicly published, standard algorithms used by default: Ed25519 (ed25519-dalek), ChaCha20-Poly1305, Argon2id, SHA-256 (sha2) — all well-reviewed public algorithms, confirmed present as dependencies in Cargo.toml.
crypto_call_justification: Cryptography is delegated to dedicated crates (ed25519-dalek, chacha20poly1305, argon2, sha2) rather than reimplemented; verified via `grep` in src/engines/security.rs (`SigningKey::from_bytes`, use of these crate APIs) — no hand-rolled cipher/hash code found.
crypto_floss_justification: All crypto dependencies (ed25519-dalek, chacha20poly1305, argon2, sha2) are FLOSS crates published on crates.io under permissive licenses, buildable with only FLOSS tools (Cargo/rustc).
crypto_keylength_justification: Ed25519 uses 256-bit keys and ChaCha20-Poly1305/Argon2id use 256-bit keys, both meeting NIST-equivalent strength minimums well beyond 2030; no shorter key length is offered as default.
crypto_working_justification: SECURITY.md confirms defaults are Ed25519 signing, ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD, Argon2id KDF, SHA-256 hashing — none of MD4/MD5/single-DES/RC4/Dual_EC_DRBG, and ChaCha20-Poly1305 is an AEAD mode (not a broken block-cipher mode).
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Project uses SHA-256 (not SHA-1) per SECURITY.md and ChaCha20-Poly1305 (not CBC) for authenticated encryption; no algorithm with known serious weaknesses is used by default.
crypto_pfs_justification: Crosstalk does not implement its own network key-agreement protocol; outbound calls to model providers use `reqwest` (Cargo.toml) which relies on the underlying TLS stack for transport security. No custom key-exchange code exists in src/ to evaluate for PFS.
crypto_password_storage_justification: Crosstalk has no user-account/password-authentication feature. Argon2id is used only to derive a symmetric key from an optional `CROSSTALK_SIGNING_PASSPHRASE` to encrypt the local signing seed at rest (src/engines/security.rs `derive_seed_key`), not to store login passwords.
crypto_random_justification: Signing seeds and other secrets are generated with `rand::rng().random::<[u8; 32]>()` (src/engines/security.rs lines ~170, ~513), which uses the `rand` crate's OS-seeded, cryptographically secure ThreadRng, not a non-cryptographic PRNG.
delivery_mitm_justification: README.md instructs `git clone https://github.com/dcondrey/crosstalk.git` (HTTPS) or via SSH (`git@github.com:dcondrey/crosstalk.git` per git remote), both of which counter MITM; no plain-HTTP download path is offered.
delivery_unsigned_justification: There is no hash-only integrity check distributed over plain HTTP; the only delivery channel is git over HTTPS/SSH to GitHub, and CI release artifacts (.github/workflows/ci.yml `release` job) are uploaded via GitHub's TLS-protected actions/upload-artifact.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No public vulnerability reports exist for this project (`gh issue list` and GitHub Security Advisories show none), so there is no known unpatched medium+ vulnerability outstanding; `cargo audit` runs in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml `security-audit` job) on main/tags to catch dependency CVEs.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerabilities have been reported to date; `cargo audit` and `cargo deny check` run automatically in CI on every push to main and every tag (.github/workflows/ci.yml `security-audit` job), positioned to catch and drive rapid fixes for newly disclosed advisories in dependencies.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: `.env` is listed in .gitignore and `git log --all -p -- .env` returns no history — the file was never committed. `git ls-files | grep -i env` shows only `.env.example` (a template with no real secrets) is tracked, plus source files that merely reference an 'environment' concept, not credentials.
static_analysis_justification: clippy (a FLOSS static analyzer for Rust) is run on every push/PR via `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: clippy's default lint set includes correctness and suspicious-pattern lints relevant to common bug/vulnerability classes (e.g. integer/format/unsafe misuse), and `cargo audit` (in the same CI security-audit job) specifically scans for known-vulnerable dependency versions via the RustSec advisory database.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CI fails the build on any clippy warning (`-D warnings`) and on any `cargo audit`/`cargo deny` finding (.github/workflows/ci.yml), so medium+ findings block merges by construction; CHANGELOG.md also records a past commit 'fix all clippy warnings'.
static_analysis_often_justification: clippy runs on every push to any branch and every pull request (.github/workflows/ci.yml `test` job trigger: `push: branches: ['**']` and `pull_request: branches: [main]`), i.e. on every commit, not just before releases.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No dynamic analysis tool (e.g. fuzzing harness, ASan/TSan/Miri run) was found: no `fuzz/` directory, no cargo-fuzz/afl configuration, and .github/workflows/ci.yml has no sanitizer or fuzzing step.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The codebase is Rust; no significant use of `unsafe` memory-unsafe code was found as a distinct concern (WASM execution is sandboxed via wasmtime, and native code is safe-Rust by default), so memory-safety dynamic tooling for C/C++-style unsafe code is not applicable.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic-analysis run configuration exists in CI (see dynamic_analysis), so there is no assertion-enabling config to evaluate.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis tool is currently applied (see dynamic_analysis), so there are no dynamic-analysis findings to have fixed.
